correctness.rationale: For prime \(p\), the identity \(P_p(X)=S_p(X)^2+pX^{p-1}\) is independently reconstructed from the coefficient definition. Both \(P_p\) and \(H_p\) are monic of degree \(2p-2\), congruent to \((X-1)^{2p-2}\) modulo \(p\), and take value \(p(p+1)\) at \(1\); their translates are Eisenstein at \(p\). The identity \(Q_p(X)=(1+X^2)H_p(X^2)\) is verified algebraically. For \(p\equiv3\pmod4\), the sign condition \(H_p(-1)=1-p^2<0<H_p(0)\) yields a negative real root \(\alpha\) generating a real number field of degree \(2p-2\). Adjoining its square root has degree two, proving irreducibility of \(H_p(X^2)\), which has degree \(4p-4\). Finite exact checks cover primes at most 47; the proof is unrestricted.

value.rationale: Two explicit irreducibility expectations about naturally defined generalized-totient Lambert numerators are resolved on unbounded prime-index families. The first covers every prime \(p\), and the second covers the infinite congruence family \(p\equiv3\pmod4\); the quotient case requires a real-embedding obstruction beyond the Eisenstein step. This supplies a uniform arithmetic mechanism rather than a few irreducible examples, while leaving composite indices and the \(p\equiv1\pmod4\) composition honestly open.
